result.rationale: The diff adds next/previous actions that immediately set offset and call group.findMembers() with no in-flight guard (unlike save, which sets disableSave). The described race — overlapping requests where an out-of-order response's setProperties overwrites newer state — is a real mechanism visible in the new code: findMembers' then() unconditionally sets user_count/limit/offset/members from whichever response resolves last. However, whether the stale response actually arrives last depends on server timing not provable from the diff alone, so this is a plausible race with moderate confidence.

judged_text: The next/previous actions have no in-flight guard, so a second click before the first response fires a second overlapping findMembers() request and the last response to arrive wins the state. An admin who double-clicks next triggers requests for offset 50 and offset 100; when the offset-50 response arrives last its setProperties overwrite the newer state and the UI settles on page 2 after two clicks that should have reached page 3 — the displayed page silently diverges from the user's actions.
